subject_id.description: Unique identifier for the study subject.
subject_id.clinical_usage: Used for tracking patient data throughout the study, ensuring anonymity while maintaining data linkage.

related_formulas: Age (Years) = Current Date - birthdate
birthdate.clinical_usage: Used to calculate patient age, which is a critical factor in disease risk assessment, diagnosis, and treatment selection.

related_formulas: Creatinine Clearance (Cockcroft-Gault) - uses sex as a factor.
GFR estimation formulas (e.g., CKD-EPI, MDRD) - often use sex as a factor.
sex.clinical_usage: Essential for risk stratification, as disease prevalence, progression, and response to certain treatments can differ significantly between sexes.

Alcohol consumption.description: Indicates the patient's history of alcohol consumption (Yes, No, Ex-Drinker).
related_formulas: Assessment of liver injury risk (in conjunction with ALAT, ASAT, Gamma-GT).
Alcohol consumption.clinical_usage: Assessing lifestyle factors that impact cardiovascular, hepatic, and neurological health.

Other addictive behaviors.description: Binary indicator for other addictive behaviors (likely 1=Yes, 0=No).
Other addictive behaviors.clinical_usage: Identifying co-occurring risk factors that may complicate treatment or influence overall prognosis.

Smoking.description: Patient's current or past smoking status (No, Former smoker, Active smoker).
related_formulas: Calculation of Pack-Years (if smoking history is detailed).
Risk assessment for cardiovascular disease (e.g., Framingham Risk Score components).
Smoking.clinical_usage: Major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, chronic lung disease, and cancer. Used for risk assessment and counseling.

ALAT.description: Measurement of the enzyme ALAT, often used as a marker for liver function.
related_formulas: De Ritis Ratio (ASAT/ALAT) - Parameter.
Assessment of liver injury/inflammation.
ALAT.clinical_usage: Primary marker for hepatocellular injury. Elevated levels suggest liver damage from various causes (e.g., viral hepatitis, fatty liver, drug toxicity).

Albumin to creatinine ratio.description: Ratio used to screen for kidney damage (albuminuria).
related_formulas: Diagnosis/Staging of Diabetic Nephropathy (Microalbuminuria/Proteinuria assessment) - Result.
Albumin to creatinine ratio.clinical_usage: Key screening tool for diabetic nephropathy and general chronic kidney disease (CKD). Microalbuminuria (elevated UACR) is an early sign of glomerular damage.

ALP.description: Measurement of the ALP enzyme, often related to liver or bone health.
related_formulas: Assessment of liver function/bone turnover.
ALP.clinical_usage: Used to screen for liver disease (especially cholestasis/bile duct obstruction) and bone disorders (e.g., Paget's disease, osteomalacia).

ASAT.description: Measurement of the enzyme ASAT, often used as a marker for liver function.
related_formulas: De Ritis Ratio (ASAT/ALAT) - Parameter.
Assessment of liver injury.
ASAT.clinical_usage: Used alongside ALT to assess liver injury. A high AST/ALT ratio can suggest alcoholic liver disease or cirrhosis.

Cholesterol total.description: Measurement of total cholesterol, likely in one unit (e.g., mg/dL or mmol/L).
related_formulas: Friedewald Equation (LDLc calculation) - Parameter.
Total Cholesterol (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).
Cholesterol total.clinical_usage: Part of the standard lipid panel used to assess overall cardiovascular risk. The unit must be known (mmol/L or g/L) for interpretation.

Cholesterol total.1.description: Measurement of total cholesterol, likely in a different unit than the first instance.
related_formulas: Friedewald Equation (LDLc calculation) - Parameter.
Total Cholesterol (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).
Cholesterol total.1.clinical_usage: Used for overall cardiovascular risk assessment.

Cholesterol total.2.description: Indicates the unit used for total cholesterol measurement (mmol/L or g/L).
related_formulas: Conversion: Total Cholesterol (g/L) to (mmol/L). Standard conversion factor for Cholesterol is $\text{mmol/L} = \text{mg/dL} / 38.67$ or $\text{mmol/L} = \text{g/L} / 100 * 38.67$. Assuming g/L and mmol/L are the primary units:
Conversion: $1 \text{ g/L} \approx 25.86 \text{ mmol/L}$ (using molecular weight of Cholesterol $\approx 386.65 \text{ g/mol}$)
Cholesterol total.2.clinical_usage: Essential for correctly interpreting the numerical value of Total Cholesterol.

CPK.description: Measurement of the CPK enzyme, often a marker for muscle damage.
related_formulas: Assessment of muscle damage (e.g., rhabdomyolysis, statin side effects).
CPK.clinical_usage: Used to diagnose muscle injury (rhabdomyolysis) or myocardial infarction (though less specific than troponin).

Creatinine.description: Measurement of creatinine, a marker for kidney function.
related_formulas: Cockcroft-Gault Equation (CrCl) - Parameter.
CKD-EPI GFR Equation - Parameter.
MDRD GFR Equation - Parameter.
UACR calculation (if UACR is not directly measured, though here it is listed separately).
Creatinine.clinical_usage: Primary marker for estimating Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) and assessing current kidney function.

Fasting glycemia.description: Measurement of blood glucose after a period of fasting.
related_formulas: Estimated Average Glucose (eAG) from HbA1c - Parameter.
HOMA-IR calculation - Parameter.
Fasting glycemia.clinical_usage: Essential for the diagnosis and monitoring of diabetes mellitus and prediabetes.

Fasting HbA1c.description: Average blood glucose level over the preceding 2-3 months (Context reference 63).
related_formulas: Estimated Average Glucose (eAG) = (HbA1c * 28.15) - 46.7 - Result.
Diagnostic criteria for Diabetes Mellitus.
Fasting HbA1c.clinical_usage: The gold standard for assessing long-term glycemic control in patients with diabetes.

Fasting insulinemia.description: Measurement of insulin levels after a period of fasting.
related_formulas: HOMA-IR = (Fasting Insulinemia * Fasting Glycemia) / 22.5 (if units are $\mu U/mL$ and $mg/dL$) - Parameter.
Fasting insulinemia.clinical_usage: Used to assess endogenous insulin secretion and diagnose insulin resistance (often calculated with glucose to determine HOMA-IR).

GFR.description: Estimated GFR, a key measure of kidney function.
related_formulas: Staging of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) - Result.
GFR.clinical_usage: The primary measure for staging and monitoring Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD).

Haematocrit.description: Percentage of blood volume occupied by red blood cells.
related_formulas: Calculation of Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV) - Parameter (requires RBC count).
Assessment of anemia.
Haematocrit.clinical_usage: Used to diagnose anemia (low Hct) or polycythemia (high Hct). Relevant in chronic disease states like heart failure or kidney disease.

HDLc.description: Measurement of High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol, likely in one unit.
related_formulas: Friedewald Equation (LDLc calculation) - Parameter.
HDL Cholesterol (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).
HDLc.clinical_usage: A component of the lipid panel; higher levels are generally protective against atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.

HDLc.1.description: Measurement of High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol, likely in a different unit.
related_formulas: Friedewald Equation (LDLc calculation) - Parameter.
HDL Cholesterol (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).

HDLc.2.description: Indicates the unit used for HDL cholesterol measurement (mmol/L or g/L).
related_formulas: Conversion: HDL Cholesterol (g/L) to (mmol/L).
Conversion: $1 \text{ g/L} \approx 25.86 \text{ mmol/L}$ (using molecular weight of Cholesterol $\approx 386.65 \text{ g/mol}$)
HDLc.2.clinical_usage: Essential for correct interpretation of the HDLc value.

hsTnT.description: Highly sensitive measurement of cardiac troponin T, a marker for myocardial injury.
related_formulas: Risk stratification in Acute Coronary Syndromes (e.g., HEART score modification, specific diagnostic thresholds).
hsTnT.clinical_usage: Used for the rapid and sensitive diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and risk stratification in heart failure patients.

LDH.description: Measurement of the LDH enzyme, often related to tissue damage.
related_formulas: Assessment of tissue damage/cell turnover.
LDH.clinical_usage: A non-specific marker of tissue damage or cell turnover. Can be elevated in hemolysis, liver disease, or advanced malignancy.

LDLc.description: Measurement of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol, likely in one unit.
related_formulas: LDLc (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).
LDLc.clinical_usage: Primary target for lipid-lowering therapy (statins). Elevated levels strongly correlate with increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).

LDLc.1.description: Measurement of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol, likely in a different unit.
related_formulas: LDLc (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).
LDLc.1.clinical_usage: Used for cardiovascular risk assessment and management.

LDLc.2.description: Indicates the unit used for LDL cholesterol measurement (mmol/L or g/L).
related_formulas: Conversion: LDL Cholesterol (g/L) to (mmol/L).
Conversion: $1 \text{ g/L} \approx 25.86 \text{ mmol/L}$ (using molecular weight of Cholesterol $\approx 386.65 \text{ g/mol}$)
LDLc.2.clinical_usage: Essential for correct interpretation of the LDLc value.

related_formulas: Diagnosis/Severity assessment of Heart Failure (e.g., cut-off values for HFpEF/HFrEF) - Result.
NT-proBNP.clinical_usage: The primary biomarker for diagnosing and risk stratifying heart failure (HF). Higher levels indicate greater severity of HF.

Platelets.description: Count of platelets in the blood.
related_formulas: Calculation of Mean Platelet Volume (MPV) - Parameter (requires platelet distribution width).
Platelets.clinical_usage: Assesses hemostatic status. Thrombocytopenia (low count) can be seen in advanced liver disease or certain inflammatory states.

Triglycerides.description: Measurement of triglycerides, likely in one unit.
related_formulas: Friedewald Equation (LDLc calculation) - Parameter.
Triglycerides (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).
Triglycerides.clinical_usage: Part of the lipid panel. Severely elevated levels (>500 mg/dL or >5.6 mmol/L) increase the risk of acute pancreatitis.

Triglycerides.1.description: Indicates the unit used for triglyceride measurement (mmol/L or g/L).
related_formulas: Friedewald Equation (LDLc calculation) - Parameter.
Triglycerides (Unit 2) conversion - Result (if unit conversion is needed).

Triglycerides.2.description: Measurement of triglycerides, likely in a different unit.
related_formulas: Conversion: Triglycerides (g/L) to (mmol/L). Standard conversion factor for Triglycerides (assuming average MW $\approx 885.4 \text{ g/mol}$ for typical plasma triglycerides):
Conversion: $1 \text{ mmol/L} \approx 0.885 \text{ g/L}$ or $1 \text{ g/L} \approx 1.13 \text{ mmol/L}$
Triglycerides.2.clinical_usage: Essential for correct interpretation of the Triglyceride value.

us-CRP.description: Measurement of hs-CRP, a marker of systemic inflammation.
related_formulas: Risk stratification for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD) (High-sensitivity CRP).
us-CRP.clinical_usage: Used primarily to assess low-grade chronic inflammation and as an independent predictor of future cardiovascular events, even in normolipidemic individuals.

Gamma-GT.description: Measurement of the GGT enzyme, often related to liver or bile duct issues.
related_formulas: Assessment of cholestasis or alcohol-related liver injury.
Gamma-GT.clinical_usage: Highly sensitive marker for chronic heavy alcohol use and for detecting bile duct obstruction or liver injury.

Fat mass.description: Body composition measurement representing total fat mass.
related_formulas: Body Fat Percentage = (Fat Mass / Total mass) * 100 - Result.
Fat mass.clinical_usage: Used in body composition analysis to assess obesity and metabolic risk, often more informative than total weight alone.

Lean mass.description: Body composition measurement representing total non-fat mass.
related_formulas: Appendicular Skeletal Muscle Mass (ASMM) calculation (if limb measurements are available) - Parameter.
Lean mass.clinical_usage: Used in body composition analysis. Low lean mass can indicate sarcopenia, especially relevant in chronic disease.

Skeletal muscle index.description: Index derived from body composition analysis, often related to sarcopenia assessment.
related_formulas: Skeletal Muscle Index (SMI) = ASMM / (Height^2) - Result (if ASMM is derived from Lean Mass).
Skeletal muscle index.clinical_usage: The standardized measure used to diagnose sarcopenia, particularly in older adults or those with chronic illness.

related_formulas: Body Mass Index (BMI) = Weight (kg) / (Height (m))^2 - Parameter.
Body Fat Percentage = (Fat mass / Total mass) * 100 - Parameter.
Total mass.clinical_usage: Fundamental vital sign used for calculating BMI, assessing nutritional status, dosing medications, and monitoring fluid status (e.g., in heart failure).

A.description: Echocardiography parameter, likely related to mitral annulus velocity (e.g., early diastolic velocity component).
related_formulas: Assessment of Left Ventricular function.
A.clinical_usage: Part of the assessment of diastolic function, specifically atrial contribution to ventricular filling.

COsimpson.description: Myocardial strain measurement calculated using the Simpson's method, likely circumferential strain.
related_formulas: Global Strain analysis of LV function - Result.
COsimpson.clinical_usage: A sensitive measure of myocardial contractility, often used to detect subclinical systolic dysfunction before changes in Ejection Fraction (EF) are apparent.

Dt.description: Time interval measured during diastole in cardiac assessment.
related_formulas: Assessment of Diastolic Function (e.g., relation to E/A ratio).
Dt.clinical_usage: Used in Doppler studies to assess ventricular relaxation and filling dynamics.

E.standard_name: Mitral Inflow Early Diastolic Velocity (E wave)
E.description: Peak early diastolic mitral inflow velocity measured by Doppler echocardiography.
related_formulas: E/A Ratio = E / A - Result.
Myocardial Relaxation Assessment.
E.clinical_usage: Represents early passive filling of the left ventricle. Crucial component in assessing diastolic function (E/A ratio).

EA.description: Ratio of mitral inflow velocity (E) to tissue Doppler velocity (A), used for diastolic function assessment.
related_formulas: Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) E/A Ratio - Result (often used for diastolic grading).
EA.clinical_usage: A key index for grading diastolic dysfunction severity, reflecting the pressure gradient between the atrium and ventricle during early diastole.

EDPWT.description: Thickness of the left ventricular posterior wall in diastole.
related_formulas: Assessment of Left Ventricular Hypertrophy/Remodeling.
EDPWT.clinical_usage: Used to assess left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) when combined with septal thickness and LVEDD.

EDSWT.description: Thickness of the interventricular septum in diastole.
related_formulas: Assessment of Left Ventricular Hypertrophy/Remodeling.
EDSWT.clinical_usage: Used to assess left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and remodeling.

EFsimpson.description: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction calculated using the Simpson's method.
related_formulas: Classification of Heart Failure (HFrEF vs HFpEF) - Result.
EFsimpson.clinical_usage: The standard clinical measure for assessing global left ventricular systolic function. Used for diagnosis and management of heart failure (HFrEF vs. HFpEF).

LA-LS-conduit.description: Strain measurement of the left atrium during the conduit phase of filling.
related_formulas: Comprehensive Diastolic Function Assessment - Result.
LA-LS-conduit.clinical_usage: A sensitive marker of left atrial function, often impaired early in diastolic dysfunction.

LA-LS-contract.description: Strain measurement of the left atrium during atrial contraction.
related_formulas: Comprehensive Diastolic Function Assessment - Result.
LA-LS-contract.clinical_usage: Assesses the active contribution of the left atrium to ventricular filling.

LA-LS-res.description: Strain measurement of the left atrium during the reservoir phase of filling.
related_formulas: Comprehensive Diastolic Function Assessment - Result.
LA-LS-res.clinical_usage: The most commonly reported measure of left atrial mechanical function, highly correlated with filling pressures and prognosis in HF.

latE'.standard_name: Lateral Annulus Early Diastolic Velocity (e' lateral)
latE'.description: Tissue Doppler velocity of the lateral mitral annulus in early diastole.
related_formulas: Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) E/e' Ratio = E / (0.5 * latE' + 0.5 * septE') - Parameter (used for LV filling pressure estimation).
latE'.clinical_usage: Reflects myocardial relaxation velocity. Used in conjunction with Mitral E velocity to assess diastolic function.

LAV_ES_al.standard_name: Left Ventricular Area at End Systole (Area method)
LAV_ES_al.description: Left ventricular area at end systole, likely calculated using the area method.
related_formulas: Assessment of Left Ventricular volume changes.
LAV_ES_al.clinical_usage: Used in older methods for calculating Ejection Fraction, though volume methods are now preferred.

LAV_ES_simpson.standard_name: Left Ventricular Volume at End Systole (Simpson's method)
LAV_ES_simpson.description: Left ventricular end-systolic volume calculated using the Simpson's method.
related_formulas: Assessment of Left Ventricular volume changes.
LAV_ES_simpson.clinical_usage: Essential for calculating Ejection Fraction (EF = (LVEDV - LVESV) / LVEDV).

LVEDD.description: Diameter of the left ventricle at the end of diastole.
related_formulas: Calculation of Relative Wall Stress (RWS) - Parameter.
Calculation of LV Mass Index (if indexed to height).
LVEDD.clinical_usage: Used to assess left ventricular chamber size and dilation, a key feature in dilated cardiomyopathy or volume overload.

LVEDV.description: Volume of the left ventricle at the end of diastole.
related_formulas: Stroke Volume (SV) = LVEDV - LVESV - Parameter.
Cardiac Index (CI) = SV / Body Surface Area (BSA) - Parameter.
LVEDV.clinical_usage: Used to assess ventricular preload and calculate Ejection Fraction.

LVESV.description: Volume of the left ventricle at the end of systole.
related_formulas: Stroke Volume (SV) = LVEDV - LVESV - Parameter.
LVESV.clinical_usage: Used to calculate Ejection Fraction and assess systolic performance.

related_formulas: Stroke Volume (SV) $\approx \pi * (LVOT/2)^2 * LVOT VTI$ - Parameter.
LVOT.clinical_usage: Used in conjunction with the velocity time integral (VTI) to calculate stroke volume (Stroke Volume = (pi * (LVOT/2)^2) * LVOT VTI).

LVOT VTI.standard_name: Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Velocity Time Integral (VTI)
LVOT VTI.description: Integral of the velocity profile across the LVOT, used to calculate stroke volume.
related_formulas: Stroke Volume (SV) $\approx \pi * (LVOT/2)^2 * LVOT VTI$ - Parameter.
LVOT VTI.clinical_usage: Used to calculate stroke volume and cardiac output. Essential for assessing aortic valve function.

RV-GLS.description: Global longitudinal strain measurement of the right ventricle.
related_formulas: Assessment of Right Ventricular function - Result.
RV-GLS.clinical_usage: A sensitive, emerging marker for assessing right ventricular function, often impaired in pulmonary hypertension or left-sided heart disease.

septE'.standard_name: Septal Annulus Early Diastolic Velocity (e' septal)
septE'.description: Tissue Doppler velocity of the interventricular septum in early diastole.
related_formulas: Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) E/e' Ratio = E / (0.5 * latE' + 0.5 * septE') - Parameter (used for LV filling pressure estimation).
septE'.clinical_usage: Reflects myocardial relaxation velocity. Used in conjunction with Mitral E velocity to assess diastolic function.

TR Vmax.description: Maximum velocity of tricuspid regurgitation jet, used to estimate pulmonary artery pressure.
related_formulas: Estimation of Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure (PASP) using Bernoulli equation: $PASP \approx 4 * (TR Vmax)^2 + CVP$ - Parameter.
TR Vmax.clinical_usage: Used in the simplified Bernoulli equation (Pressure Gradient = 4 * Vmax^2) to estimate the pressure gradient between the right atrium and right ventricle, which is used to estimate Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure (PASP).

GCS_ap.description: Global strain measurement derived from apical views (likely longitudinal strain).
related_formulas: Global Strain analysis of LV function - Result.
GCS_ap.clinical_usage: Used to quantify regional or global myocardial deformation in specific imaging planes.

GCS_bas.description: Global strain measurement focused on the basal segment of the ventricle.
related_formulas: Global Strain analysis of LV function - Result.
GCS_bas.clinical_usage: Used to assess myocardial deformation, often reflecting the most affected segment in certain cardiomyopathies.

GCS_mid.description: Global strain measurement focused on the mid segment of the ventricle.
related_formulas: Global Strain analysis of LV function - Result.
GCS_mid.clinical_usage: Used to assess myocardial deformation in the mid-wall region.

GLS-2CH.description: Global Longitudinal Strain calculated from the 2-chamber echocardiographic view.
related_formulas: Global Longitudinal Strain (Averaged GLS from multiple views) - Parameter.
GLS-2CH.clinical_usage: A measure of overall left ventricular systolic function, often more sensitive than EF, especially in early cardiotoxicity or HFpEF.

GLS-3CH.description: Global Longitudinal Strain calculated from the 3-chamber echocardiographic view.
related_formulas: Global Longitudinal Strain (Averaged GLS from multiple views) - Parameter.
GLS-3CH.clinical_usage: A measure of overall left ventricular systolic function.

GLS-4CH.description: Global Longitudinal Strain calculated from the 4-chamber echocardiographic view.
related_formulas: Global Longitudinal Strain (Averaged GLS from multiple views) - Parameter.
GLS-4CH.clinical_usage: A measure of overall left ventricular systolic function.

COVID19 results.description: Result of the COVID-19 test (negative or positive).
COVID19 results.clinical_usage: Used to classify patients based on current or past infection status, which may influence cardiovascular risk or management.

Basal Insulin.description: Binary indicator for the use of basal insulin (likely related to diabetes management).
related_formulas: Total Daily Dose (TDD) calculation (if used with mealtime insulin).
Basal Insulin.clinical_usage: Used to classify the intensity of diabetes management regimen.

Type 2 diabetes diagnosis - Year.description: The year the patient was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes.
related_formulas: Duration of Diabetes = B0 VISIT DATE - Year of Diagnosis - Result.
Type 2 diabetes diagnosis - Year.clinical_usage: Used to calculate the duration of diabetes, a key factor in assessing cumulative risk for micro- and macrovascular complications.

Sleep Apnea Syndrome - History.description: Binary indicator for a history of Sleep Apnea Syndrome.
related_formulas: Risk factor assessment for cardiovascular disease/hypertension.
Sleep Apnea Syndrome - History.clinical_usage: Sleep apnea is a significant comorbidity associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and worsening heart failure.

Calcium Channel Blockers.description: Binary indicator for the use of Calcium Channel Blockers.
related_formulas: Polypharmacy scoring systems.
Calcium Channel Blockers.clinical_usage: Used to manage hypertension, angina, and certain arrhythmias.

Dyspnea (NYHA).description: New York Heart Association functional classification related to dyspnea (I, II, III).
related_formulas: Heart Failure severity classification - Result.
Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLWHFQ) scoring.
Dyspnea (NYHA).clinical_usage: Standard clinical measure of the severity of heart failure symptoms related to exertion.

Metformin (biguanides).description: Binary indicator for the use of Metformin (a biguanide class drug for diabetes).
related_formulas: Assessment of T2DM treatment regimen.
Metformin (biguanides).clinical_usage: Used to assess the patient's diabetes treatment regimen and adherence.

Beta-blockers.description: Binary indicator for the use of Beta-blockers.
related_formulas: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) assessment for HF/CAD.
Beta-blockers.clinical_usage: Cornerstone therapy for hypertension, angina, post-myocardial infarction, and heart failure (specific agents).

Sulfonamides.description: Binary indicator for the use of Sulfonamide class drugs (often antidiabetic or antibiotic).
related_formulas: Assessment of T2DM treatment regimen (less common).
Sulfonamides.clinical_usage: Assessing medication history, particularly relevant for potential drug allergies or specific diabetes treatment pathways.

related_formulas: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) = DBP + 1/3 * (SBP - DBP) - Parameter.
Risk stratification for hypertension/CVD.
Diastolic blood pressure.clinical_usage: Used to diagnose and monitor hypertension. Important for assessing cardiovascular risk.

related_formulas: Body Mass Index (BMI) = Weight (kg) / (Height (m))^2 - Parameter.
Weight.clinical_usage: Fundamental vital sign used for BMI calculation, nutritional assessment, and medication dosing.

GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.description: Binary indicator for the use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (antidiabetic medication).
related_formulas: Assessment of T2DM treatment regimen (cardio-protective agents).
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.clinical_usage: Modern injectable therapy for T2DM, often chosen for its cardiovascular and weight-loss benefits.

Fibrates.description: Binary indicator for the use of Fibrates (lipid-lowering medication).
related_formulas: Management of hypertriglyceridemia.
Fibrates.clinical_usage: Used in the management of severe hypertriglyceridemia.

Loop Diuretics.description: Binary indicator for the use of Loop Diuretics.
related_formulas: Assessment of fluid overload/Heart Failure management.
Loop Diuretics.clinical_usage: Primary treatment for symptomatic volume overload in acute and chronic heart failure.

Potassium Sparing Diuretics.description: Binary indicator for the use of Potassium-Sparing Diuretics.
related_formulas: Assessment of Heart Failure management (often in combination with RAAS inhibitors).
Potassium Sparing Diuretics.clinical_usage: Used in hypertension and heart failure; often used as mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) in HF management.

Diabetic feet - History.description: Binary indicator for a history of diabetic foot issues.
related_formulas: Assessment of long-term diabetic complications.
Diabetic feet - History.clinical_usage: Indicates severe, long-standing microvascular complications and high risk for future morbidity.

Ankle swelling.description: Binary indicator for the presence of ankle swelling (edema).
related_formulas: Clinical sign of fluid retention/Heart Failure exacerbation.
Ankle swelling.clinical_usage: A common sign of fluid retention, often associated with worsening heart failure, venous insufficiency, or kidney disease.

Other origin.description: Specific details regarding non-European/African geographic origins.
Other origin.clinical_usage: Used for granular epidemiological analysis, potentially revealing regional differences in disease prevalence or genetic background.

Microalbuminuria.description: Binary indicator for the presence of microalbuminuria (early kidney damage).
related_formulas: Staging of Diabetic Nephropathy (if UACR is not available or used for confirmation).
Microalbuminuria.clinical_usage: Crucial screening marker for diabetic nephropathy and cardiovascular risk.

DPP-4 Inhibitors.description: Binary indicator for the use of DPP-4 Inhibitors (antidiabetic medication).
related_formulas: Assessment of T2DM treatment regimen.
DPP-4 Inhibitors.clinical_usage: Oral agents for T2DM, generally considered weight-neutral and cardiovascular-neutral (though some data exists).

Hip.description: Measurement related to hip size, possibly circumference or a bone density measure.
related_formulas: Calculation of Waist-to-Hip Ratio (WHR) - Parameter.
Hip.clinical_usage: Used as a measure of central adiposity, often combined with Waist Circumference to assess visceral fat distribution.

LV_peak_systolic_rad_strain.standard_name: Left Ventricular Peak Systolic Radial Strain
LV_peak_systolic_rad_strain.description: Peak systolic strain measured radially in the left ventricle.
related_formulas: Global Strain analysis of LV function - Result.
LV_peak_systolic_rad_strain.clinical_usage: Assesses regional or global myocardial contractility, particularly useful for evaluating concentric hypertrophy or ischemia.

Statins.description: Binary indicator for the use of Statins (lipid-lowering medication).
related_formulas: ASCVD risk reduction therapy assessment.
Statins.clinical_usage: Primary therapy for lowering LDL cholesterol and reducing atherosclerotic cardiovascular event risk.

SGLT-2 Inhibitors.description: Binary indicator for the use of SGLT-2 Inhibitors (antidiabetic medication).
related_formulas: Assessment of T2DM treatment regimen (cardio-renal protective agents).
SGLT-2 Inhibitors.clinical_usage: Modern T2DM therapy with proven benefits in reducing heart failure hospitalization and cardiovascular death, independent of glycemic control.

Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.description: Binary indicator for the presence of PND, a symptom of heart failure.
related_formulas: Clinical sign of fluid overload/Heart Failure exacerbation.
Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.clinical_usage: A specific and highly suggestive symptom of acute or worsening congestive heart failure.

LV_peak_systolic_circ_strain.standard_name: Left Ventricular Peak Systolic Circumferential Strain
LV_peak_systolic_circ_strain.description: Peak systolic strain measured circumferentially in the left ventricle.
related_formulas: Global Strain analysis of LV function - Result.
LV_peak_systolic_circ_strain.clinical_usage: A sensitive measure of myocardial contractility, often the first strain parameter to decline in early cardiac dysfunction.

Orthopnea.description: Binary indicator for the presence of orthopnea, a symptom of heart failure.
related_formulas: Clinical sign of fluid retention/Heart Failure severity.
Orthopnea.clinical_usage: A classic sign of elevated left atrial pressure and fluid redistribution, strongly indicative of heart failure.

CARDIATEAM group.description: Classification based on Type 2 Diabetes and Heart Failure with preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF) status.
related_formulas: Stratification based on T2DM and HFpEF status - Result.
CARDIATEAM group.clinical_usage: Used to stratify patients into distinct clinical phenotypes for targeted research analysis (e.g., Group 3: T2DM without HFpEF; Group 4: T2DM with HFpEF).

Glitazones.description: Binary indicator for the use of Glitazones (thiazolidinediones, antidiabetic medication).
related_formulas: Assessment of T2DM treatment regimen.
Glitazones.clinical_usage: Insulin sensitizers for T2DM. Can cause fluid retention, requiring caution in patients with heart failure.

Reduced exercise tolerance.description: Binary indicator for the presence of reduced exercise tolerance.
related_formulas: Clinical sign related to NYHA classification or functional capacity.
Reduced exercise tolerance.clinical_usage: A general indicator of functional limitation, often related to cardiac, pulmonary, or metabolic impairment.

related_formulas: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) = DBP + 1/3 * (SBP - DBP) - Parameter.
Risk stratification for hypertension/CVD.
Systolic blood pressure.clinical_usage: Used to diagnose and monitor hypertension. A major modifiable risk factor for stroke and myocardial infarction.

Retinopathy.description: Binary indicator for the presence of retinopathy (likely diabetic retinopathy).
related_formulas: Assessment of long-term diabetic complications.
Retinopathy.clinical_usage: A microvascular complication indicating cumulative end-organ damage from hyperglycemia/hypertension.

Thiazides.description: Binary indicator for the use of Thiazide diuretics.
related_formulas: Assessment of hypertension management.
Thiazides.clinical_usage: First-line agents for the management of uncomplicated hypertension.
